content_voiceover: G6PD deficiency is X-linked recessive, gene at Xq28, thirteen exons, and there are over four hundred described variant enzymes, making it the most common red cell enzyme disease worldwide, capable of causing both extravascular and intravascular hemolysis. The WHO classification is built entirely around residual enzyme activity. Class I is severe, under ten percent activity, and rare, but it's the one that causes chronic hemolysis even without a trigger. Class II is also severe, under ten percent, common in Mediterranean and Asian populations, and causes intermittent hemolysis. Variants here include Mediterranean, Kaiping, Gaohe, and Chinese-3. Class III is moderate, ten to sixty percent activity, seen in Africa and Southeast Asia, causing intermittent hemolysis only under stress. This includes the A- variant, found in about ten percent of Africans, and the Canton variant. Class IV has near normal activity, sixty to one-fifty percent, no hemolysis, the wild-type B and A+ variants. Class V is over one-fifty percent activity, essentially no clinical relevance. For boards with a Taiwan or Asian population focus, remember Canton, a G1376T mutation, accounts for about fifty percent of G6PD deficient Taiwanese males, with Kaiping second at roughly twenty-one percent.
keypoints: X-linked recessive, Xq28, >400 variants — most common RBC enzymopathy
Class I: <10% activity, rare, chronic hemolysis even without trigger
Class II: <10% activity, Mediterranean/Asian, intermittent hemolysis
Class III: 10-60% activity, African A- and Canton, stress-triggered hemolysis
Canton variant most common in Taiwanese males (~50%)
keypoint_voiceover: Bottom line for boards. G6PD deficiency is X-linked, Xq28, the most common red cell enzymopathy. Class I is rare but causes chronic hemolysis with under ten percent activity. Class II, also under ten percent, causes intermittent hemolysis and includes the Mediterranean and Kaiping variants. Class III is moderate, ten to sixty percent activity, includes African A- and the Canton variant, and only hemolyzes under stress. Classes IV and V have normal or increased activity and no disease. In Taiwan, Canton is the dominant variant.
